---

The capture gate and the capture itself each run their own pre-flight, so a finding can land that
the gate never reported.

`scripts/graph-capture.py` runs `sdd new --dry-run`, reads the severities out of that output, and
refuses anything above low. It then runs `sdd new`, which runs its own pre-flight. The validator asks
a model, so the two runs answer independently. An entry can therefore capture carrying a medium
finding the gate never saw, which is what `d-tac-nd9` did.

The gate itself works. Its pattern matches the severity line in the real output, and a rerun over the
same draft reports the medium and refuses it. Only the second evaluation escapes the check.

The cost is a silent one. A reader trusts that a captured entry cleared the gate, and the entry's own
capture output carries the finding, which nobody reads again once the capture succeeds.

Two repairs are available, and this signal picks neither. The capture could refuse when its own
output carries a finding above low. That leaves the entry written, and the operator supersedes it.
The gate could instead capture in one step, parsing the real run rather than a rehearsal.
